public_case.title: Rare/less common: spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD)

symptoms: Acute chest pain after intense emotional stress; discomfort persists for 30 minutes.
No known prior coronary disease. Scenario includes a recent major stressor; it is a clue, not proof of SCAD.
history: Pregnancy/postpartum history must be asked when relevant, not assumed

reference_findings.safety_review: Do not make the simulator imply all SCAD requires PCI. Emphasize clinical stability, expert review, associated-condition assessment and monitored care decisions.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: expert review favours SCAD; no automatic PCI is performed in the stable synthetic branch. If instability is introduced, route to urgent specialist escalation.
learning_objectives: Recognize a non-atherosclerotic cause of ACS.
Avoid equating every angiographic narrowing with plaque.
Discuss why intervention decisions differ by mechanism.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
